text:
maria: Heads up — saw a spike of OOMs on gpu-pool-3 last night, ~02:14 UTC. pattern: long seqs + simultaneous warm KV scans. attaching profiler link and a tiny log snippet.

evan: thanks. any perf regressions noted in last deploy? kernel selector changes?

maria: yes, we rolled kernel-splitter v2.1.5 + prefetch heuristics at 01:45. perf diff was positive for p95 previously but mem footprint for KV windows jumped.

leo: can you paste the minimal stack/log? i want to see allocator trace.

maria: copy: ```
[02:14:03] alloc failed: requested 320MB, free 12MB -> soft-oom
[02:14:03] kvcache: trying eviction (forced)
[02:14:03] kernel-switch: selected path "fused-attn-qual" seq=2048 batch=1
[02:14:04] OOM: fallback to small-quant variant triggered
``` 

aj: looks like two things coincided: kernel choice favored fused path with larger temporary workspace, and our KV prefetch queued several cold shards increasing resident set. we should consider two mitigations: 1) a transient kernel demotion (prefer mem-slim kernel under KV pressure) 2) request shaper + short-circuit cache prefetch when free mem < threshold.

sre_oncall: can we do a quick canary rollback to kernel-splitter v2.1.4 on a subset? that'll prove if selector is the culprit.

evan: +1. propose: deploy rollback to canary pool (gpu-pool-3a) and enable a runtime circuit that refuses prefetch when free_gpu_mem_pct < 8%.

maria: created quick action plan and a tiny playbook in thread:
- step 1: switch canary kernels on pool-3a (rollback to 2.1.4)
- step 2: runtime flag: `kv_prefetch.enabled_if_free_pct>=8` (hotfix)
- step 3: enable kernel-demotion policy: prefer `mem-slim` when total_kv_resident_mb > 6GB
- step 4: enable soft-fail to small-quant variant earlier (reduce retry delay to 50ms)

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: rollback job 98532 queued to gpu-pool-3a

leo: for longer-term: we should surface a selector score that combines estimated workspace + live_kv_allocations. current selector looks only at latency/cost.

aj: agree. also add a transient buffer-reuse limiter: when we detect >2 concurrent sequences >1500 tokens, cap per-request scratch to 128MB.

maria: i'm going to run a flamegraph and an allocator timeline. linking: https://internal.perf/graphs/3123456789-oom-profile

evan: nice. can we add an observability alert: when OOM rate > 3 in 10m for a pool, automatically switch to conservative kernel routing and engage prefetch circuit? low-friction automated mitigation.

sre_oncall: making a pager action: if auto-mitigation triggers, page oncall + post to #incidents with a short summary. non-blocking unless mitigations fail after 5m.

leo: small test patch i'd like to try: selector fallback ordering uses `workspace_estimate + kv_resident_weight*kv_live_mb`. weight can be tuned; start with 0.6.

aj: include a telemetry tag `oom-mitigation:kernel-demote-v1` when we demote so we can aggregate outcomes.

maria: ACTIONS:
- evan: roll canary rollback and flip prefetch flag (in 10m)
- leo: add selector score change PR and canary rule (TBR)
- aj: add buffer-reuse limiter and telemetry tag
- evan/sre_oncall: add alert + auto-mitigation playbook to console

maria: tl;dr: immediate rollback + prefetch circuit should stop the OOM cascade; longer term we'll make selector memory-aware and introduce runtime soft-fallback wiring.

evan: on it, will update status in thread. :thumbsup:

runtime-bot: canary rollback completed on gpu-pool-3a (job 98532) — health checks passed

maria: initial telemetry: OOMs on pool-3 dropped to 0 within 6 minutes of canary flip. keeping the rest of rollout paused until final PRs merge.

leo: saved the flamegraph snapshot to the perf board and wrote notes. planning follow-up RFC for selector memory awareness.

aj: I'll open the PR for buffer limiter + telemetry today.

maria: great work team. we'll formalize this as a small playbook for future similar incidents (kernel + kvcache interactions).
